headline: Evidence, Integrity and Cyber Risk
thesis: A Dartmouth provost's resignation over AI use and calls for proof behind classroom AI pauses push education toward accountability — while AI-enhanced phishing raises the security stakes.
summary: Coverage this week centers on accountability for AI. Inside Higher Ed reports Dartmouth's provost resigned after a faculty review found he used AI to meaningfully alter his writing, and columns argue assessment must be redesigned and that learning science should guide AI decisions. EdSurge asks whether AI pauses protect students or leave some behind, noting 82% of teachers have never had formal AI guidance. EdTech Magazine cites a CDW report that 43% of higher ed respondents faced AI-enhanced phishing. Ed-Fi's state data stories and November 9–11 Summit, plus 1EdTech's November 12 session on what GenAI must prove, keep evidence and interoperability in view.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · OCTOBER 30, 2026 · Search-snippet based; ETI, ISTE, Brookings and THE Journal had no items dated this week, and EdTech Week's October event has concluded.
